title: On Discovering the door behind the shelf
subtitle: 科学探索 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 科学探索（科学与技术·科学精神、科学探究）
meta: 主题语境：科学探索（科学与技术·科学精神、科学探究）　|　核心词汇：discover　|　正文 338 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 discover 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1985 the director ① discovered the door behind the shelf in public, and every actor in the theatre said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three nights on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the director ② discovers the door behind the shelf in silence without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ discover the door behind the shelf at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ discovered the door behind the shelf before — a line in the poster for August 1979 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Discovering the door behind the shelf in public, the director said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the script at the far stage, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ discover the mistake too late in silence, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Discover the mistake too late at once and never mention it again.

By 1992 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the poster, and a new actor from the next theatre ⑧ discovers the mistake too late in public every night without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the stage, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ discovered the door behind the shelf again when nobody else would.

⑩ To discover the door behind the shelf, my mother said in 1997, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the theatre remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the theatre forgets, somebody discovers the door behind the shelf in silence again and somebody must discover the door behind the shelf in public all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 发现（一般过去式 discovered the door behind the shelf：1985 年导演头一回这样做，当着众人面）
B. v. 发现（一般现在 discovers the door behind the shelf：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 发现（不定式 to discover the door behind the shelf：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 发现（过去完成时 had discovered the door behind the shelf：1979 年八月的戏报上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 发现（动名词 discovering the door behind the shelf 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 发觉（discover the mistake too late：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去发觉发觉那个错时为时已晚）
G. v. 发觉（discover the mistake too late：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 发现（后段两处：新来的演员照例 discovers the mistake too late，而母亲又一次 discovered the door behind the shelf）

discover 意为“发现”，自那以后导演一言不发地把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 discovers。
discover 意为“发现”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯发现发现书架后面那道门”，此处为不定式 to discover the door behind the shelf。
discover 意为“发现”，戏报里 八月 那行字说明早在 1992 年之前就有人发现过，故用过去完成时 had discovered。
discover 意为“发现”，导演说“发现发现书架后面那道门这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 discovering the door behind the shelf 作主语。
discover 意为“发觉”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去发觉发觉那个错时为时已晚”，should ever 之后用原形 discover the mistake too late。
discover 意为“发觉”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻发觉发觉那个错时为时已晚（discover the mistake too late at once），以后再也不要提起。
discover 意为“发现”，新来的演员每个夜晚都照例发觉发觉那个错时为时已晚，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 discovers。
discover 意为“发现”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次当着众人面发现发现书架后面那道门，用一般过去式 discovered 叙述。
discover 意为“发现”，结尾那句是母亲 1997 年的话：要发现发现书架后面那道门，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和戏院记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 discover 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1985 the director discovered the door behind the shelf in public, and nobody in the theatre forgot it.
Even now the director discovers the door behind the shelf in silence whenever the theatre asks.
Discovering the door behind the shelf in public, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever discover the mistake too late in silence, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new actor from the next theatre discovers the mistake too late in public every night, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother discovered the door behind the shelf again, and the theatre remembered that half.
